title: Casper and the Oath
premise: Casper Vale is a memory-thief who keeps the ledgers of the Ashgrove Guild, an organization that trades in impossible things — stolen years, borrowed names, forgotten debts. When he finds tonight's date inscribed in a century-old book of prophecies, he is pulled bodily into the prophecy itself: a country called Vell that was erased from every map and memory, existing now only inside the pages of stolen recollections. To escape, Casper must find the Door Out of Vell before the country finishes forgetting itself, guided by Yara Ashgrove, the guild's exiled heir who erased her own homeland to save it. In the end, Casper learns the prophecy requires a keeper to remain behind holding Vell's memories; he chooses to stay, becoming the living ledger of a nation no one will ever remember, while Yara carries his final memory — her own name spoken with love — back through the Door.
about_author: Jude Reyes is the pen name of a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing unclaimed heirlooms in a coastal city's records office. They write fantasy about paperwork, memory, and the quiet violence of being forgotten.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: POV Casper. In the Ashgrove Guild's vault, Casper audits entries for traded memories and notices one ledger page bleeding ink that shouldn't exist. He steals a sliver of a stranger's memory to test it and sees a door standing alone in a wheat field. Emotional beat: restless competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Tonight's Date
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Cross-checking the anomalous entry against the Prophecy Codex, Casper finds tonight's exact date written a century ago, describing 'the keeper who counts.' The guildmaster dismisses it; the codex's margins begin rewriting themselves around Casper's name. Beat: dread arriving as bureaucracy.

chapters.title: Pulled
chapters.summary: POV Casper. At midnight the vault folds inward like a closing book, and Casper falls through the codex into Vell — a country of perpetual dusk where citizens repeat the same day without noticing. He meets Yara Ashgrove, who has been waiting a hundred years for the keeper. Beat: vertigo and unwilling wonder.

chapters.title: A Country That Isn't
chapters.summary: POV Yara. Yara explains Vell was erased from maps and minds by the Oath its own founders swore to survive a plague of forgetting; only the guild's ledgers preserve it. She needs Casper because the Door Out opens only for someone recorded in both worlds. Beat: guilt worn as authority.

chapters.title: Citizens of Dusk
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper witnesses Vell's loop firsthand: a baker relives her daughter's funeral daily, unaware. His thief's instinct flares — he could steal her grief and free her — but Yara warns that every theft accelerates the country's unraveling. Beat: compassion versus survival.

chapters.title: The Guild's Debt
chapters.summary: POV Yara. Flashback chapter: young Yara helped her father write the Oath, trading Vell's existence to the Codex in exchange for sparing its people from the plague. She has spent a century unable to enter or leave. Beat: the price of survival made personal.

chapters.title: Ink and Iron
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The Oath's enforcers — the Blank, faceless clerks who erase what they touch — hunt the intruder written in the Codex. Casper hides in the archive-cathedral and discovers his own ledger page growing longer each hour he stays. Beat: hunted, and complicit.

chapters.title: What Thieves Keep
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Cornered, Casper steals a Blank's memory and learns the horrifying truth: the Blanks are former keepers who stayed too long and were emptied. He tells Yara nothing. Beat: fear curdling into secrecy.

chapters.title: The Wheat Field Door
chapters.summary: POV Yara. Yara leads Casper toward the Door from his first vision, but it stands in a field that remembers being burned. Crossing requires a payment of equal weight: something loved. Casper offers a stolen childhood memory; the Door refuses it as not truly his. Beat: first failure.

chapters.title: Yara's Empty Room
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Sheltering in Yara's preserved house, Casper finds a room scrubbed of all trace of her — she erased herself from Vell's memory to move freely. He realizes she has no one left who remembers her at all. Beat: intimacy through violation of privacy.

chapters.title: The Second Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Yara. Yara reveals a hidden second ledger listing everyone the Oath consumed to power itself — including Casper's predecessor, the last keeper, whose final entry reads 'tell her.' Yara never learned who 'her' was. Beat: hope entangled with grief.

chapters.title: A Day Worth Stealing
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper breaks his own rule and gives the baker a single remembered day with her daughter, bought with one of his own true memories. The loop stutters; the whole country shivers. Yara is furious; the citizens briefly wake. Beat: kindness with consequences.

chapters.title: The Blank Court
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Captured, Casper is brought before the Blank Court, which offers him a bargain: leave now, forget Vell entirely, and live. He almost takes it — until he hears the court speak in his predecessor's voice. Beat: temptation rendered as mercy.

chapters.title: Tell Her
chapters.summary: POV Yara. Rescued by Yara, Casper confesses what he heard. Yara realizes 'her' was her — the predecessor was her father's partner, and the message was never delivered. Her century of exile reframes as abandonment she chose. Beat: devastating recontextualization.

chapters.title: Rewriting the Oath
chapters.summary: POV Yara. In the archive-cathedral, they study the original Oath and find a flaw: it demands a keeper, but never specified which world the keeper must remember from. A loophole exists — if someone outside Vell willingly holds its memory. Beat: strategy kindled by love.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: POV Casper. To carry Vell out, Casper must take in every citizen's name and story — thousands of stolen-feeling memories — knowing each will displace part of himself. He begins the rite, losing his mother's face first. Beat: sacrifice measured in increments.

chapters.title: The Country Wakes
chapters.summary: POV Yara. As Casper absorbs Vell, the loop breaks; citizens wake mid-day, terrified, remembering everything. Some curse the thieves; some beg to forget again. The Blanks converge on the cathedral. Beat: liberation that feels like catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Door Stands Open
chapters.summary: POV Casper. At the wheat field, the Door finally opens — but the Codex's fine print surfaces: the keeper must remain inside Vell to anchor what was taken. Casper hides this from Yara and lies beautifully, as thieves do. Beat: love and deception in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Oath Kept
chapters.summary: POV Yara. Yara sees through the lie — she wrote the same lie a century ago. They fight, then stop fighting. She offers to stay instead; Casper refuses, arguing a keeper must be someone the ledgers already trust. Beat: the argument that is really a farewell.

chapters.title: One Memory Left
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper performs the final transfer, emptying himself into Vell's restoration. He keeps exactly one memory against the rules: Yara's name, spoken aloud once, freely given. The Door holds open for her alone. Beat: quiet, enormous choice.

chapters.title: The Keeper Who Counts
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Alone in a Vell reborn under real morning light, Casper becomes its living ledger, greeting waking citizens with their returned names. The Blanks dissolve, released. He begins counting — days, names, small mercies. Beat: sorrow transfigured into purpose.

chapters.title: Ashgrove
chapters.summary: POV Yara. Through the Door, Yara returns to the guild carrying Casper's last memory and the truth of Vell. She reopens the ledgers, writes him into history as more than a prophecy, and vows to find a way back. Final line echoes the codex: the keeper counts, and someone counts the keeper. Beat: grief braided with resolve.
